patterns.title: Contract-mediated component access
patterns.status: mandatory owner-selected component-boundary policy; application realization remains a design decision
patterns.when: A call crosses an approved component boundary; internal collaborator calls are outside this requirement.
invariants: Expose the approved contract. Keep implementation details behind the boundary.
Apply all permitted and prohibited interactions in C-SD-4, C-SD-5, and C-SD-6.
Use cohesive business operations. Do not expose property-like service operations.
Apply the current Microsoft technical standard and owner-selected unprefixed naming to derived implementations. Preserve historical reference files unchanged.
Route every cross-component call through a DI-capable contract proxy.
Generate a typed local proxy when no service-level separation exists.
Do not implement a reflection-based proxy.
Keep internal collaborator calls outside the mandatory proxy scope.
implementation_choices: Select a service invocation proxy or generate a typed local proxy according to the approved separation.
Dapr sidecar service invocation is an accepted realization; Dapr is not mandated or deployed.
Specify injected chain collaborators, order, registrations, lifetimes, cancellation, and failure behavior in the detailed design.
verification: Review actual dependency edges, including indirect calls.
Test contract behavior and failure paths through the boundary.
Verify that callers do not require the concrete service implementation.
Reject direct implementation or direct registration bypasses.
Verify that a local boundary uses generated typed forwarding and that proxy dispatch does not use reflection.
Test actual DI resolution and call-chain order, not just interface presence.

patterns.title: Service contract inheritance with proxy chaining
patterns.status: candidate; not selected for an application
patterns.when: A reviewed contract has a justified inherited capability, and the selected technology supports the pattern.

sources.availability: Historical review record only; original source copy removed from vc.Governance.
Historical review record only; original source copy removed from vc.Governance.

invariants: Keep inheritance aligned with cohesive public capabilities. Do not grow a contract merely to reuse implementation code.
Preserve the source sample attribution and license when using its code.
Do not mistake proxy class inheritance for permission to change component dependency rules.
Apply the current Microsoft technical standard and owner-selected unprefixed naming to derived implementations. Preserve historical reference files unchanged.
implementation_choices: The sample chains the scientific proxy through the simple proxy; the simple proxy uses a channel typed to the scientific contract.
Evaluate this channel coupling explicitly. Do not infer that the base proxy is independent of derived contracts.
Treat the sample as historical evidence, not a production-ready runtime selection.
verification: Test inherited and added operations through their intended public interfaces.
Verify endpoint and contract compatibility, channel cleanup, and fault behavior.
Evaluate contract metrics over the effective exposed operation set.

patterns.title: Generated infrastructure around approved components
patterns.status: candidate; not selected for an application
patterns.when: Repeated infrastructure behavior has a stable, reviewed definition.

sources.availability: Historical review record only; original source copy removed from vc.Governance.

invariants: Keep business decisions in the approved business components.
Do not use generated infrastructure to add forbidden dependencies or silently change contracts.
Keep generation inputs and templates outside implementation-worker amendment authority.
Apply the current Microsoft technical standard and owner-selected unprefixed naming to derived implementations. Preserve historical reference files unchanged.
implementation_choices: Compare generation, composition, decorators, interception, and rewriting under the approved baseline. No mechanism is selected by this catalog.
Record generator version, approved input revision, and generated output ownership.
Make regeneration reproducible and generated behavior inspectable. These controls are proposed framework mechanisms, not quotations from Lowy.
verification: Regenerate from the same inputs and compare outputs.
Test observable behavior, exception paths, and required infrastructure presence.
Verify that disabling or replacing a generator cannot silently bypass integration checks.

patterns.title: Explicit message-type registration
patterns.status: candidate; not selected for an application
patterns.when: An approved boundary transmits polymorphic message types.

sources.locator: Section 2.3.2 and 2.4.1, printed pp. 50–55; PDF pp. 75–80
sources.availability: Historical review record only; original source copy removed from vc.Governance.

invariants: Define the permitted message family in the contract design.
Do not let discovery expand the public message surface without design approval.
Treat runtime discovery as implementation of an approved type policy, not authority to invent that policy.

patterns.title: Failure containment at approved boundaries
patterns.status: candidate; not selected for an application
patterns.when: Availability requirements identify a risk of dependency failure propagation.
invariants: Retain volatility-based component decomposition.
Specify business-correct failure behavior. Do not report fabricated success.
Contain failures through existing permitted boundaries; do not create architecture bypasses.
implementation_choices: Evaluate weak links, bounded dependency behavior, fallback, and redundancy against explicit failure scenarios.
The Solution Architect selects mechanisms and resource costs; developers cannot introduce new platform dependencies independently.
verification: Inject the approved dependency failures in the designated test environment.
Measure propagation, recovery, and contractual responses against explicit acceptance criteria.
Test interactions of individually healthy components as well as isolated component failures.

patterns.title: Controlled failure learning
patterns.status: candidate; not selected for an application
patterns.when: The system has approved failure-containment and recovery behavior.
invariants: Use findings to propose reviewed corrections. Do not let a learning loop rewrite architecture or policy.
Keep experiments within approved environments and impact limits.
Route fixes through the existing lifecycle and design owners.
implementation_choices: The Test Architect specifies fault scenarios, containment preconditions, stopping conditions, and recovery checks.
QA records recurring causes and proposes process improvements within the assigned authority.
verification: Record the injected fault, observed impact, recovery, and resulting corrective work.
Demonstrate that the same failure is detected after the correction.
Do not label a system anti-fragile merely because it survives one experiment.

patterns.title: Reusable fractal business nodes
patterns.status: candidate; not selected for an application
patterns.when: Business analysis establishes a recurring participant structure and canonical interaction.

sources.locator: Printed/PDF pp. 4–8; Figures 1 and 2 on p. 7

invariants: Design the participant structure and canonical interaction before multiplying nodes.
Keep regular Method constraints inside each node.
Keep participation opt-in and specify behavior when a node operates alone or disconnects.
Do not infer unrestricted component-level upward or sideways calls from business-level participant interactions.
implementation_choices: Evaluate a common node implementation with differences expressed through approved resources and constrained behavior configuration.
Model level-specific communication and legacy interoperability nodes.
Treat configuration and simulation as designed capabilities; constrain who can amend behavior and which contracts it may invoke.
verification: Simulate alternative structures and representative interactions before selecting a topology.
Test identical node logic in different levels and participant configurations.
Test disconnection, reconnection, and partial structures.
Verify that configurable behavior cannot invoke unapproved dependencies.

patterns.when: Business, system, or service requirements are recorded for design and test handoff.

sources.locator: Sections on requirement identifiers, source linking, traceability matrix, and language quality
sources.authority: supporting article: Donn Le Vie, Jr.

sources.locator: Chapter 4; Appendix A, printed pp. 388–390; C-SD-1

invariants: Record behavior and its business source. Do not disguise a proposed design as a requirement.
Distinguish system-level Software Requirements Specification from service-level SRS in the lifecycle.
Preserve guideline modality in the framework; do not replace every SHOULD with SHALL because a requirements-writing article discourages weak requirement language.
implementation_choices: Use stable IDs, requirement scope, source, conditions, expected behavior, acceptance criteria, owner, and revision.
Trace reviewed requirements to detailed designs, test plans, work items, and verification evidence.
Maintain traceability as design and construction progress; do not require all implementation links before design begins.
verification: Check identifier uniqueness and valid revision links.
Review business meaning and testability with the Product Owner and responsible architect.
Check that service requirements and test plans refer to the same reviewed scope.

patterns.title: Purpose-driven UI data visualization
patterns.status: candidate; owner approved the supporting reference for UI usage; no application realization selected
patterns.when: An approved UI requirement needs users to understand or explore data.

sources.locator: Chapter 2, pp. 15–17; Chapter 3, pp. 21–24; Chapter 4, pp. 25–29; Appendix B, pp. 91–93
sources.authority: supporting UI design guidance: Noah Iliinsky and Julie Steele, 2011
sources.availability: Historical review record only; original source copy removed from vc.Governance.

invariants: State the user information need before choosing a chart or visualization tool.
Keep UI composition within approved component and contract boundaries.
Do not use visualization convenience to authorize Client-to-Engine calls or multiple Manager calls for one use case.
Preserve source meanings: distinguish hue from ordered brightness or saturation.
Keep supporting UI guidance distinct from Method directives.
implementation_choices: Specify audience, context of use, relevant data dimensions, relationships, units, and intended comparisons.
Choose visual encodings that match data type, order, and distinguishable values.
Keep meanings consistent across related views; use additional encoding channels when they improve comprehension.
Specify labels and vocabulary for the intended reader.
Record data-state and interaction requirements in the reviewed detailed design; see ui-visualization.md.
verification: Have the Product Owner assess whether representative readers can answer the intended question.
Check encoded values, labels, units, ordering, and relationships against representative data.
Test distinguishability and consistency on the intended display conditions.
Test empty, unavailable, partial, and extreme data states as specified by the detailed design.
Verify that filtering or selection respects approved contracts and dependency rules.

patterns.title: Attribute-driven method I/O tracing
patterns.status: owner-required capability; detailed mechanism not yet selected or implemented
patterns.when: A method is decorated with the designated tracing attribute, regardless of public, internal, or private accessibility.

sources.locator: Read-only review of existing service logging and Roslyn constraints
Selected owner-identified experimental proxy, context, DI, status, telemetry, and redaction source snapshot
sources.authority: confirmed implementation reference; reflective dispatch is not adopted
sources.availability: Historical review record only; original source copy removed from vc.Governance.

invariants: Automatically trace inputs and outputs for attributed public, internal, and private methods.
Do not implement reflection-based method dispatch or proxying.
Preserve method semantics and diagnose unsupported forms.
Keep internal method instrumentation distinct from inter-component proxies.

Alternative requiring an authoring convention: generator-created wrapper and explicitly separated implementation.
Use current approved logging APIs; source-generated logging helpers do not by themselves instrument a business method.
verification: Exercise actual public, internal, and private method calls including private self-calls.
